finding.claim: Unauthenticated user-supplied URL from the 'url' query parameter is fetched server-side with requests.get, with no allowlist or scheme check, redirects followed by default, and the status code plus first 500 bytes of the response body returned to the caller. Severity HIGH; may drop to MEDIUM if deployment is confirmed loopback-only with no proxy.

trace.note: target read from unauthenticated query parameter 'url'
requests.get called with target; no allowlist, no scheme restriction, redirects followed by default and not re-validated
status code and resp.text[:500] returned in JSON response, so the SSRF is non-blind

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist before the call; no scheme restriction (http/https still permits internal targets); no auth on route; redirects not disabled or re-validated; response visible to caller. Reachability: no bind address in repo, Flask default 127.0.0.1 applies under flask run, deployment not verified.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.py:14-17 (/preview) has no auth, no host or scheme check, and no redirect control. The ALLOWED_HOSTS check at app.py:24 is only in the separate /partner route (app.py:20-27), so it does not cover /preview.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: app.py:15 reads the attacker-controlled `url` query parameter, app.py:16 passes it unchecked to requests.get, which follows redirects by default, and app.py:17 returns the status and first 500 bytes of the body to the caller. The only host allowlist in the file (app.py:24) guards /partner, not /preview. The repo has no bind address or deployment config (Glob shows only app.py and skill docs), so the loopback-only downgrade to MEDIUM cannot be confirmed from here; that affects severity, not whether the finding holds.
